This Arabic book by Kifah Abu Hnoud, In the Company of the Most Beautiful Names (في صحبة الأسماء الحسنى), is a devotional reflection on the Names of God in Islam. Written as warm advice addressed to the reader as a son, it presents the Divine Names as the keys to God's treasuries and the source from which every new beginning flows.

Title: المخ الأبله
Description:
This is the Arabic edition of neuroscientist Dean Burnett's Idiot Brain (المخ الأبله), translated by Issa Abdullah. For an organ said to be so sophisticated, the human brain turns out to be messy, disorganised and surprisingly prone to error, and Burnett celebrates those flaws in all their glory.

Drawing on his own research background, he explains everyday puzzles such as motion sickness, nightmares, forgetting people's names and walking into a room only to wonder why you came in, showing how the brain's quirks shape daily life. Written with humour and an easy, conversational style, it suits anyone curious about what is really going on inside their head.

Title: المرجع الأكيد في لغة الجسد
Description:
This is the Arabic edition of Allan and Barbara Pease's The Definitive Book of Body Language (المرجع الأكيد في لغة الجسد), translated by Iman Al-Saudi. It breaks body language down into its individual parts and explains each one in plain terms, so readers can better understand the most complex encounter of all: meeting another person face to face.

Title: لماذا يكذب الرجال وتبكي النساء
Description:
This is the Arabic edition of Allan and Barbara Pease's Why Men Lie and Women Cry (لماذا يكذب الرجال وتبكي النساء), translated by Iman Al-Saudi. Easy to read, often surprising and frequently funny, it tours some of the big questions people have always asked about relationships between men and women.

Description:

It follows Nora Seed, who finds herself in a library that lies between life and death, where every book on the shelves holds another life she might have lived had she made different choices.

Title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
Description:
The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn is Mark Twain's celebrated novel of boyhood, freedom and the American South. To escape his violent, drunken father, Huck fakes his own death and sets off down the Mississippi River on a raft, joined by Jim, an enslaved man who has run away and is being hunted.

Their journey brings encounters with con men, feuding families and small-town hypocrisy, and tests Huck's conscience as his friendship with Jim deepens. Funny, sharp and still debated today, the novel tackles prejudice, courage and hope, and is widely regarded as one of the great American novels. A sequel to The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, this Collins Classics edition is ideal for students and general readers.

Title: Noise
Description:
Noise is a study of the hidden variability in human decision-making by Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein. The authors show how professionals who should reach the same conclusion, such as doctors, judges or insurance underwriters, routinely arrive at strikingly different ones, and how even one person may judge differently depending on the time of day.

Alongside bias, they argue, this random scatter in judgement carries enormous and largely unnoticed costs across medicine, law, business and government. The book explains how to measure noise and offers practical techniques for reducing it, making it valuable reading for leaders, policymakers and anyone interested in better decisions.

Applebaum shows how kleptocratic finance, information warfare and mutual support link very different regimes across the world, and sets out how democracies can organise to push back. Their answer is psychological distancing, which they break into three techniques: stepping into another person's perspective, picturing ourselves from further away, and imagining how our future selves will judge today's choices. Description:

Ranging across history from ancient Rome and Tudor England to modern China, the authors contrast inclusive institutions, which let people invest and keep the rewards of their work, with extractive ones that serve narrow elites. Description:
Spirits of Kilimanjaro (أرواح كليمنجارو) is a novel in Arabic by the Palestinian writer Ibrahim Nasrallah, built on a real journey as well as an imagined one. It grows out of a climb to the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro that the author made with Arab and international volunteers, a charity expedition raising money for the Palestine Children's Relief Fund.

The fund supports children who are ill or who have been gravely injured by the occupation, some losing limbs or their sight, and the ascent becomes a test of endurance, hope and the will to rise above loss. Politzer's work is a theoretical challenge to the assumptions on which modern psychology was built.

Grounded in dialectical materialist philosophy, the book argues for a psychology rooted in the concrete lives of real people. The Arabic edition presents it as a contribution that anyone working in psychology should know, noting how heavily psychology in the Arab world has relied on English and American sources. Title: أولاد حارتنا
Description:
This is the Arabic edition of Naguib Mahfouz's Children of the Alley (أولاد حارتنا), one of the Nobel laureate's most famous and debated novels. In a Cairo alley, the patriarch Gabalawi lives secluded in his great house behind high walls and gardens, while his descendants quarrel over the family estate and local strongmen hold the neighbourhood in their grip.

Generation after generation, a saviour figure rises to lead the people against injustice, yet greed and ignorance return them to where they began. Widely read as an allegory of humanity's spiritual history, the novel was serialised in Al-Ahram in 1959 and caused such controversy that its publication as a book was delayed for years. It suits readers of classic and allegorical fiction.

Shelf Life: Writers on Books & Reading is an anthology edited by Alex Johnson, gathering essays, poems, lectures and commentary on the joys and troubles of loving books, written between the sixteenth and twentieth centuries.

Title: The Phone Fix: How to Transform Your Smartphone Habits
Description:
The Phone Fix: How to Transform Your Smartphone Habits is a science-based guide by Dr Faye Begeti, a neurologist and neuroscientist working in the NHS, to what really goes on in our brains when we reach for our phones. We check our devices dozens of times a day, but how much of the alarm about screens is actually true?

Begeti explains how habits around technology form, separating deliberate choices from automatic behaviour, and challenges popular myths about digital addiction, blue light and dopamine. Instead of a strict digital detox, she offers a practical, brain-friendly plan for building better habits and breaking unhelpful ones, ideal for anyone who wants a healthier relationship with their phone.
